description.narrative:
Mozambique’s agricultural transformation hinges on one decisive factor: farmers’ access to quality seed of improved, climate-resilient varieties. Despite strong agro-ecological potential and rising demand, the seed sector remains constrained by weak coordination, underperforming regulation, limited basic seed supply, and an underdeveloped private sector. Farmers depend on a mix of seed systems, making a coherent, system-wide approach essential.
For the Netherlands, this is a strategic opportunity. Seed sector transformation is a proven entry point to deliver on food and nutrition security, private sector development/ engagement and climate resilience, core priorities of Dutch foreign and development policy. MSP builds directly on more than fifteen years of Dutch leadership in seed sector transformation in Ethiopia, Uganda, Rwanda and Nigeria, applying the Integrated Seed Sector Development (ISSD) approach. Mozambique is ready to become the next flagship, positioning the Netherlands at the centre of a high-impact, system-wide reform agenda.
The program’s goal is to ensure farmers gain reliable access to quality seed at scale. It does so by simultaneously strengthening all seed systems, professionalising entrepreneurs and agro-dealers, and reforming the enabling environment. Operating nationally across farmer-managed, local enterprise, public–private, and international systems, MSP ensures that investments in regulation, research, and markets reinforce one another. Its 16 Action Pathways provide a structured, results-driven framework for implementation.
MSP is designed for impact and visibility. Embedded within existing EKN-funded regional programs, it directly strengthens value chains, climate-smart agriculture, SME growth, and farmer resilience in priority provinces. At the same time, it delivers national-level reform, modernising quality assurance, accelerating variety release, improving seed planning, and transitioning from subsidy-driven approaches to sustainable market systems. This dual model positions MSP as a backbone program: linking Dutch-funded field investments to lasting national reform.
Critically, MSP creates tangible opportunities for the Dutch private sector. By improving regulatory transparency, strengthening plant variety protection, and reducing barriers to market entry, it enables Dutch seed companies to invest, innovate, and scale in a high-potential market. A dedicated public–private partnership facility supports companies to introduce and adapt varieties, build local partnerships, and expand distribution. This aligns commercial interests with development outcomes, creating a credible pipeline from Dutch innovation to Mozambican markets.
The program is implemented through a Mozambican–Dutch partnership between the Zambezi Agency, IIAM, and Wageningen University & Research. A co-leadership model ensures national ownership while embedding Dutch expertise. Governance is anchored in MAAP, supported by a multi-stakeholder Advisory Board. Through the Dutch Diamond approach, public, private, knowledge, and regulatory actors are aligned; supported by institutions such as SeedNL and Naktuinbouw.
For MAAP, MSP provides what is currently missing: the capacity to turn policy into implementation at scale. For the Netherlands, it offers a high-visibility, high-leverage investment that delivers on development goals while opening markets for Dutch expertise and enterprise.
An investment of €12.5 million over five years unlocks substantial co-financing from Mozambican institutions, existing Dutch programs, research organisations, and the private sector. This blended model maximises impact, reduces duplication, and ensures sustainability.
MSP is more than a program; it is a strategic partnership. It positions the Netherlands as a long-term partner in Mozambique’s agricultural transformation, delivering measurable results for farmers, creating opportunities for Dutch businesses, and demonstrating global leadership.
